# MM-P2-L4-HP03 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Scope
This manual provides removal, inspection, torque verification, reinstallation, and acceptance criteria for the main ram bolt and hydraulic system verification on Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). It applies to preventive and corrective maintenance activities performed on the press at Plant P2, line P2-L4. For design changes, modifications, or field engineering requests, refer to ECN-2026-042. For safety bulletins and retrofit advisories, consult SB-1007. For normal operating lockout and procedural prerequisites, see SOP-P2-L4-01.

Background and rationale
The main ram bolt secures the ram assembly to the actuating interface and is a primary structural fastener. Correct bolt preload is essential to prevent relative movement, fatigue cracking, and alignment shift that can cause tooling damage or hydraulic failure. Hydraulic system overpressure or underperforming reliefs can induce dynamic loads on the bolted joint beyond the original design assumptions. Verifying both mechanical torque and system pressure limits ensures the assembly operates within safe envelopes and maintains uptime.

Critical values
- The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m.
- The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar.

Tools and materials
Required tools include certified torque wrench calibrated and traceable to lab standards, impact wrench for removal where allowed by procedure, thread cleaning tools, torque extension adapters as needed, non-ferrous alignment drift, anti-seize compound where specified, and personal protective equipment consistent with SB-1007 and SOP-P2-L4-01. Prepare inspection mirrors and dye penetrant kit for fastener and adjacent surface inspection.

Procedure
Preparation
- Review SOP-P2-L4-01 for lockout-tagout and machine isolation steps prior to any mechanical access. Verify documentation of isolation in the maintenance log.
- Inform operations and schedule downtime through the plant maintenance coordinator per local rules.

Removal and inspection
- Remove covers to access the main ram bolt as described in the equipment schematics and job aids.
- Clean the bolt and mating surfaces to allow visual and nondestructive inspection. Use dye penetrant on the bolt shank and head seating area where accessible.
- Inspect for thread damage, head rounding, corrosion, or evidence of yield. If damage is present, submit a replacement request using ECN-2026-042 and do not reuse the bolt.

Thread preparation and lubrication
- Clean threads in the nut and bolt using specified solvents and wire tools. Remove all debris.
- Apply anti-seize compound only where specified by the equipment manufacturer. Excess compound on torque shoulders or on threads beyond the specified area will invalidate the torque outcome.

Reinstallation and torqueing
- Begin hand-starting the nut to ensure proper thread engagement and alignment. Use non-impact tools for final alignment steps.
- Using a calibrated torque wrench, apply the main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) to the specified value: 1575 N·m.
- If a torque sequence is required to maintain flange parallelism, follow the sequence described in the equipment assembly drawing and tighten in incremental passes to the final torque using the calibrated instrument.
- Record the torque wrench calibration identifier and the applied torque value in the maintenance record.

Hydraulic system check
- Confirm hydraulic fluid levels and filter condition per OEM recommendations prior to pressurization.
- With pressure sources isolated, perform a controlled pressure test. Ensure system controls and reliefs are functional and verify that system pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03): 320 bar.
- Monitor for leaks, pressure fluctuations, or unusual noises during the test. If pressure attempts to exceed the limit, stop and bleed system pressure, then investigate relief valves and pilot circuits. Reference SB-1007 for additional safety considerations.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If the torque wrench indicates slippage or inconsistent readings while attempting to apply 1575 N·m, stop and verify tool calibration and mechanical condition of the wrench. Do not proceed until the measurement tool is verified.
- Example: If during pressurization the system tops at a value near but below 320 bar and then slowly rises, suspect relief valve drift or thermal expansion. Document findings and request an engineering assessment under ECN-2026-042 if adjustments are necessary.

Records to keep
- Complete the Maintenance Activity Record with: maintenance technician name, equipment id EQ-P2-L4-HP03, pre- and post-maintenance condition notes, the exact applied torque 1575 N·m, the hydraulic test result noting that system pressure did not exceed 320 bar, torque wrench calibration id, and references to SOP-P2-L4-01 and SB-1007 when relevant.
- Retain dye penetrant inspection reports and photographs in the equipment file.
- If any nonconformance is found, file a corrective action and link to ECN-2026-042 for traceability.

Acceptance criteria
- Main ram bolt is free of visible damage, correctly seated, and torqued to 1575 N·m with evidence recorded.
- Hydraulic system holds pressure without exceeding the system pressure limit of 320 bar during functional checks and exhibits no uncontrolled leaks or relief chatter.
- No unusual vibration or misalignment detected during a controlled low-force cycle as described in SOP-P2-L4-01.
- All records are complete and filed in the equipment maintenance log and electronic document control system.

References
- ECN-2026-042
- SB-1007
- SOP-P2-L4-01

Safety and remarks
Follow all lockout-tagout procedures and PPE requirements in SOP-P2-L4-01 and SB-1007. If any measured condition deviates from the values cited in this document, cease operations and escalate to engineering using ECN-2026-042 for corrective action.
